attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter, endorsed in his authorial voice.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will', conditional on the LLMs failing. The scope (workers fired by CEOs who bought the hype) and the antecedent are kept. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Reading this as a general pattern of the same workers returning is a fair plain reading. The contract rightly says that non-rehiring without a deadline cannot count as failure. Treating restored roles and returning workers as different things is an evaluator choice.

evidence.note: From 2024, before the statement. Klarna's CEO describes shrinking through attrition, not layoffs, so it doesn't show the antecedent or any rehiring.
CBA reversed 45 announced AI-related cuts, and staff could stay. That is a cancelled redundancy, not dismissal then rehiring. The 'voice-bot' isn't shown to be an LLM.
A 2026 HR survey finds many roles restored after AI layoffs. It doesn't isolate LLMs, identify returning individuals, or tie restorations to replacement failure.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm conditional forecast with no deadline. The evidence doesn't establish the full antecedent (dismissal, LLM replacement, then failure) for any identifiable group, and no rehiring of those same workers is documented. No conclusive event has occurred, so it stays open and unscored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, in his authorial voice.

semantics.note: A causal claim about why the narrative spread (clicks plus fear). The knowledge-economy qualifier is kept. The revision removed the added 'not because of evidence'.

contract.note: Reading 'everyone' as rhetorical and 'because' as a material contributing cause is fair and ordinary. Requiring evidence specific to this narrative is reasonable.

evidence.note: Upworthy experiments show negative words raise clicks in general. Not specific to AI job-loss stories or to coverage decisions in 2025.
Pew finds 52% of workers worried about workplace AI. That shows the fear exists, but not that it drove engagement with this story or more coverage.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows a general negativity-click effect and widespread worker anxiety about AI. It has no engagement data for this specific narrative and no editorial or causal evidence linking engagement rewards to repeated coverage. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence. The Mims story is mentioned only as an exception.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'I can find no stories' framing and the exception for the freelancer story.

contract.note: Reading the published claim as saying qualifying reports were absent is the ordinary reading in context. The contract requires a named business, displaced employees and described replacement work, which roughly follows his demand. The result depends on whether management-sourced detail is enough.

evidence.note: An Oct 2023 report: Dukaan laid off most of its support staff for the chatbot Lina, with tasks and metrics described. The figures come from management, not an audit.
A July 2023 report on the same Dukaan case. It notes the technical details weren't disclosed, which limits how specific the account is, though the story clearly existed.

reviews.rationale: Before June 2025, mainstream outlets carried stories naming Dukaan as having replaced most of its support employees with the Lina chatbot. They described what it handled and gave response and cost figures. That meets the contract's contradiction condition, though the details are management claims rather than independently verified.

attribution.note: Zitron's own aside, in his authorial voice.

semantics.note: Keeps 'some engineers', the speed benefit, and the limit on trusting it in production.

contract.note: Reading 'trust' as unchecked reliance fits his point about human oversight. The June 2025 window is an evaluator choice, but a reasonable one.

evidence.note: A 2022 Copilot experiment shows 55.8% faster completion. It predates the window and doesn't measure trust in production.
A company's own account of AI-generated code going to deployment after thorough human review. That is not unchecked trust, and it isn't the speaker's cohort.
A 2024 survey on trust in AI accuracy and keeping a human in the loop. Its available_at is later than the post date. It is general and doesn't cover the cohort.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows speed gains and that human review continues, but not in a cohort that ties both parts together during the target period. Reviewed production use doesn't contradict the claim under the contract's meaning of trust. The packet doesn't settle it.
